testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: With a manual transmission, how can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake to prevent rolling backward. Use the parking brake if needed.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does no spray from other vehicles mean?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is trapped under the vehicle.
The tires have soaked up all the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: When the road looks wet but other vehicles are not spraying water, ice has likely formed. Drive carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS will:

options.text: Help others see when you brake.

questions.explanation: ABS on your tractor will still help you steer better. Watch the trailer and reduce brake pressure if it begins to swing out.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, where should you set it for normal braking?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Keep the front brake limiting valve in the normal position. Research shows this valve does not improve safety, so it should stay in the normal setting.

questions.question: When must a written vehicle inspection report be signed?

options.text: Only if defects have been noted and fixed or do not need fixing.
Only if repairs will cost more than $1,000.
Only if a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects have been noted and fixed or do not need fixing.
questions.explanation: Sign the previous inspection report only if defects were found and fixed or did not need fixing.

questions.question: Most CDL drivers have ____ licenses.
questions.explanation: Most CDL drivers who operate commercial vehicles between states are non-excepted interstate commerce drivers.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Steer so all wheels are on the shoulder.
Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: Keep one set of wheels on the pavement for better control. Stop completely on the shoulder if you can, then return to the road when it is safe.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are braking?

options.text: Tap the brakes a couple of times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a couple of times.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap the brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights and warn drivers behind you.

questions.question: When going down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Before you start going down the hill
After you have already started going down
As far down the hill as possible
At the bottom of the hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going down the hill
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before starting down a hill. This helps you maintain a safe speed without using your brakes too much.

questions.question: When you approach a vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, you should look under it to check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is parked on an incline.
Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot.
Whether the vehicle is parked on a decline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle to check for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks on the ground. Leaks mean the vehicle has unsafe problems.

questions.question: Which braking system includes the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: You use the service brake system when you press the brake pedal while driving normally. It applies and releases the brakes.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must use mechanical force to work.

questions.question: Why are roads very slippery when rain first starts to fall?

options.text: Water mixes with grease and oil on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with grease and oil on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain just begins to fall. Water mixes with oil and grease on the road, creating a slick surface. As rain continues, the oil and grease wash away.

questions.question: A high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:

options.text: Use a B or C extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a B or C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: B and C type fire extinguishers work on electrical fires. Never use water on an electrical fire because it can cause electric shock.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to get it over with.
Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing, walk around your vehicle to check for hazards in your path. Use both side mirrors while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Not back up in a straight line.
Not correct drift until you are very far off course.
Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, pull forward to reposition your vehicle as needed.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will NOT be required to:

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: For your CDL, you must pass an inspection test to show your vehicle is safe. You will walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You will not have to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The brakes will not work as well as without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.explanation: If only the tractor has ABS and the trailer does not, jackknifing risk is reduced. You will still be able to steer and control the vehicle. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out.

questions.question: On a leaf spring, the leaves:
questions.explanation: Broken or missing leaves in leaf springs are dangerous. If more than one-fourth of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should not:

options.text: Expect other drivers to clear your path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect other drivers to clear your path.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spot before changing lanes. Use your turn signal. It is your job to make sure the lane is clear. Do not expect other drivers to move out of your way.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade, your brakes may fade. What happens if brakes fade?

options.text: They work differently from front to back.

questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downgrade causes them to overheat and work poorly. Use engine braking instead to avoid this problem.

questions.question: When covering cargo, a cover that flaps in transit:

options.text: Allows air to get to the cargo to keep it cool.

questions.explanation: A flapping cover can tear loose and uncover the cargo. This can block your view or the view of other drivers.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the flames.
Aim the fire extinguisher at the ground about two feet away from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from the fire as you can. Aim the extinguisher at the base of the fire.

questions.question: Failing to exit your vehicle properly during an exercise in the basic vehicle control skills test will result in:

options.text: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
An extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and use three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive above the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: On the expressway, maintain your lane position, keep proper distance from other vehicles, and drive at the speed limit. Check your mirrors regularly to watch all traffic around you.

questions.question: The air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air in storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brake system. Tanks have drains to remove these materials.

questions.question: When doing an inspection, ensure that the brake pads are:
questions.explanation: Brake shoes and pads must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is necessary to warm up parts of the engine.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.
Should be done on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration damages the vehicle.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while you drive:
questions.explanation: A flapping cargo cover can tear loose while you drive. This can uncover cargo and block your view or other drivers' views.

questions.question: In an emergency while driving, you should:

options.text: Always turn on your flashers to warn others.

questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency. Usually, steering away from danger is safer than stopping.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular roads. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when air pressure reaches 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Texting while driving a commercial vehicle is:

options.text: Acceptable if the text is work-related.
Acceptable if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing or reading text on any electronic device.

questions.question: Spring brakes engage when:

options.text: Too much air pressure is lost.
Tire tread depth is too low.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes engage automatically when air pressure drops too low. When you see the low pressure warning, safely stop your vehicle as soon as possible instead of waiting for spring brakes to engage.

questions.question: A header board is used to:

options.text: Help the driver see behind the vehicle.
Protect the driver from moving cargo.
Prevent the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board (headache rack) protects the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: If you stop on the highway, place warning devices how far behind your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your stopped vehicle on the highway.

questions.question: You should cover cargo to:
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people from spilled cargo and to protect the cargo from rain and weather.

questions.question: Which surface provides the least traction?
questions.explanation: Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice. Be extra careful when driving on melting ice.

questions.question: How should you test a parking brake?

options.text: The engine should not be running.
Put the vehicle in low gear and try to pull forward.
Have a professional mechanic inspect it.
Drive the vehicle with the parking brake applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and try to pull forward.
questions.explanation: To test a parking brake: fasten your seatbelt, set the parking brake, release the trailer brake if needed, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it needs to be fixed.

questions.question: What can cause poisonous fumes to enter the cab?

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Tires that are not fully inflated.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed on a wet road?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third on a wet road. Wet roads are slippery, making it harder to stop or turn. You must slow down to drive safely.

questions.question: What is the driver responsible for?

options.text: Finding out where the cargo came from.

questions.explanation: The driver must inspect the cargo before the trip starts, even if someone else loaded it. This is the driver's responsibility.

questions.question: What should happen when you start the engine?

options.text: Warning lights should come on and then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on and then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off within a few seconds. If they do not turn off, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: What do you need to do to inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Wear gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Chock the wheels and turn off the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and turn off the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, place wheel chocks, and turn off the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check that it moves no more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: How should a pre-trip inspection be done?

options.text: Never the same way twice in a row.
Skip it if the vehicle seems to be working well.

questions.explanation: Do the pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not forget to check anything.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed for 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, even small amounts, must have a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: How important is a vehicle's center of gravity?
questions.explanation: Keeping the center of gravity low is very important. This helps prevent the vehicle from tipping over.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that is black because of dirt on the road.
Ice that is easy to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it may look like the road is just wet.
